summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked). Research design only; no empirical values recorded. Q1 (growth accounting): Cobb-Douglas log-difference decomposition via src.economic_model.growth.growth_accounting into capital, quality-adjusted labour (employment x Mincerian human-capital index) and a TFP residual, by FY sub-period, with capital stock from perpetual inventory (growth.capital_path) on spliced NSO constant-price GFCF, steady-state initial stock and a labelled depreciation grid; capital share from 1 - labour share under three alternatives (PWT labsh, ILO SDG 10.4.1, fixed grid) because NSO compensation of employees omits self-employed income. Q2: investment rate as GFCF/GDP and GCF/GDP at current prices by FY from the same NSO release, and gross ICOR by window (inverse of investment_rate_from_icor), with unstable windows (earthquake, pandemic) flagged; results to be compared with model assumption A-TGT-05. Q3: sector GVA shares (ProductionAccounts.sector_shares) and employment shares at survey benchmark FYs, with a shift-share productivity decomposition; constant-price series spliced across the FY2000/01 -> FY2010/11 NSO rebasing by overlap-ratio splice. All computations on Nepal FY basis; WDI, ILO modelled, IMF and PWT series are cross-checks only. 26 source leads (7 located by one WebSearch in r1 or shared search-verified leads, the rest shared catalog leads or general-knowledge URLs marked unverified).

assumptions.text: Production function is Cobb-Douglas with constant returns: Y = A K^alpha (hL)^(1-alpha); decomposition by log differences, alpha constant within each sub-period. This is an accounting framework, not a causal model; TFP is a residual that absorbs measurement error, capacity utilisation and informal-sector mismeasurement.

Depreciation rate delta for the aggregate PIM is a labelled modelling assumption, not an estimate: run a sensitivity grid delta in {0.04, 0.05, 0.06} (geometric), and a fourth run using PWT 'delta' for Nepal once ingested. No value is claimed to be Nepal-specific evidence.

Initial capital stock K0 by the steady-state (Harberger) method: K0 = I0 / (g_I + delta), where I0 is the average real GFCF of the first 5 FYs of the series and g_I the average real GFCF growth over the first 10 FYs; sensitivity: K0 = capital-output ratio x Y0 using PWT rnna/rgdpna for the start year. Because the influence of K0 decays at rate (1-delta)^t, results are reported only for sub-periods starting at least 20 FYs after the series start.

Capital-share alternatives: (a) 1 - PWT labsh (Nepal, time-varying averaged by sub-period); (b) 1 - ILO SDG 10.4.1 labour income share; (c) fixed grid alpha in {0.35, 0.40, 0.50} as labelled sensitivity. NSO compensation of employees / GVA is reported but not used directly because it excludes self-employed labour income.

Annual employment between survey benchmarks is interpolated log-linearly on the employment-to-working-age-population ratio applied to 10C resident working-age paths (not WPP totals including absentees). Interpolated years are flagged 'estimate' and sub-period results are reported only between benchmark years.

Human capital index h = exp(phi(s)) with Mincerian returns piecewise as in PWT (Feenstra et al. 2015) applied to average years of schooling of the employed from NLFS/census; PWT hc used as cross-check. Quality (learning-adjusted) measures are a sensitivity only.

Splicing across NSO rebasings: level of the old-base series is rescaled by the ratio new/old in the overlap FY (ratio splice), applied separately to each ISIC section and to GFCF; interpolation splice (spreading the level discrepancy linearly over the back period) as sensitivity. The spliced series is labelled 'estimate' and never replaces the published series.

All national-accounts computations are on Nepal FY basis (mid-July, labelled by ending calendar year). Calendar-year series (WDI, ILO modelled, PWT) are used only as cross-checks, compared after an explicit documented conversion or on a year-label-mapping basis recorded from source metadata; they are never mixed into the FY computation.

ICOR computed as gross (not net) investment over real output change, as in investment_rate_from_icor; its limits (ignores depreciation, lags, utilisation, relative price of capital) are reported alongside every value.

challenges.text: Please supply, with employment by industry, the educational attainment (years of schooling or level) of the employed by survey round, and hours worked if tabulated, so labour input can be quality- and hours-adjusted consistently with the 19th ICLS concept.

Please provide resident working-age population (15-64 and 15+) on a FY-compatible basis (mid-July reference or documented conversion from 1 July), historical as well as projected, as the denominator for the employment interpolation in 01A-A05.

Register two conflicts to watch: C-new-a, NSO spliced constant-price GDP vs WDI NY.GDP.MKTP.KN vs PWT rgdpna (splicing method and year label); C-new-b, 01A PIM capital stock vs PWT rnna (delta, initial stock, asset mix). Also, NSO labour share vs PWT labsh vs ILO SDG 10.4.1 (self-employment adjustment) - methodological.

Model assumption A-TGT-05 (ICOR grid) should be re-read against 01A's historical ICOR range once computed; until then A-TGT-05 remains an unlabelled-by-evidence assumption and should not be described as historically grounded.

Hosts for NSO, WDI, PWT, ILOSTAT and IMF were unreachable in r1; all inputs for RQ-04 (real growth history) and investment/ICOR are pending. Confirm whether NSO has announced or published a new base year after FY2010/11; if so the splicing plan must add a second overlap.

uncertainty: High. No data have been retrieved in r1, so all tables are pending. Structurally: (i) TFP is a residual and inherits every measurement error in output, capital and labour; (ii) the PIM capital stock depends on the unverified depreciation rate and initial-stock method, whose influence fades only after about two decades of investment data; (iii) the capital share for a largely self-employed, agricultural labour force is poorly identified and results will be shown for three alternatives; (iv) employment exists only at a few survey benchmark years with a concept break between NLFS 2008 and 2017/18, so annual labour input is interpolated; (v) splicing across NSO rebasing introduces level and non-additivity discrepancies; (vi) ICOR is unstable in short or shock-affected windows and is a consistency check, not a production parameter. Decompositions are descriptive accounting, not causal attributions, and are not forecasts.

growth_accounting_table.question: Q1
periods: FY1975-FY1990 (if pre-2000/01 base data are retrievable)
growth_accounting_table.period_note: Sub-period boundaries are a research-design choice (conflict, reconstruction, pandemic); robustness run with fixed 5-FY windows. Periods using interpolated employment are flagged.
method: 1. Ingest NSO constant-price GDP (both bases), GFCF, GVA by industry; splice per 01A-A07 -> Y_t, I_t (NPR_const2011_mn, FY).

2. Capital: K = capital_path(k0, [I_t...], delta) from src.economic_model.growth; k0 per 01A-A03; delta grid per 01A-A02. g_K_t = ln(K_t/K_{t-1}) using beginning-of-year stock (capital services proxy).
3. Labour: L_t employment per 01A-A05; h_t per 01A-A06; g_hL = g_L + g_h.
4. Output: g_Y_t = ln(Y_t/Y_{t-1}); sub-period averages of all growth rates.

5. Decompose: growth_accounting(g_output=g_Y, g_capital=g_K, g_labour=g_hL, capital_share=alpha) per sub-period and per alpha/delta variant; labour contribution further split (1-alpha)g_L and (1-alpha)g_h.
6. Per-worker version: g_y = alpha*g_(K/L) + (1-alpha)*g_h + TFP (same function with g_labour = g_h - 0? i.e. apply to per-worker rates with capital_share alpha) for comparison with 01B comparators.
7. Cross-check with PWT 11.0 rgdpna, rnna, emp, hc, labsh, rtfpna (calendar-year labels; compare trends, not year-matched levels) and APO Productivity Databook; register discrepancies with 00B.
data_required: NSO real GDP and GVA by industry, FY2010/11 base and FY2000/01 base with overlap
NSO real GFCF (or current GFCF + GFCF deflator)
NLFS 2008, 2017/18 (and 2024/25 when published) employment and education of employed
Labour share: PWT labsh, ILO SDG 10.4.1, NSO compensation of employees if published

investment_rate_series.question: Q2
columns: GCF current NPR (GFCF + change in inventories)
investment_rate_series.period: FY2000/01 to latest FY, both NSO bases, with base marked per row
investment_rate_series.method: Ratios of current-price aggregates from the same NSO release and FY (Quantity.ratio_to enforces same unit family and period). Nominal and real investment ratios reported separately because the relative price of capital goods can move them apart. Change in inventories reported separately (can include valuables and statistical residuals in Nepal's expenditure accounts; confirm treatment in NSO methodology). ExpenditureAccounts identity check (src.economic_model.accounts) run per FY with the published statistical discrepancy supplied explicitly.
cross_checks: WDI NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, NE.GDI.FPRV.CN (year label from WDI metadata)
MoF Economic Survey appendix (later vs earlier vintage for revisions)

icor_estimate.question: Q2
icor_estimate.definition: ICOR_window = mean(GFCF_t / GDP_t, current prices) / mean(real GDP growth_t) over the window (average-ratio form, consistent with investment_rate_from_icor(real_growth, icor) = icor * real_growth). Alternative: sum(real GFCF_t-1) / (real GDP_T - real GDP_0) (lagged incremental form).
icor_estimate.excluded_or_flagged: Windows containing FY2015/16 (earthquake), FY2019/20-FY2020/21 (pandemic) or real growth near zero are flagged: ICOR is unstable when the denominator approaches zero and such windows are reported but not used for model calibration.
icor_estimate.code: Inverse of src.economic_model.growth.investment_rate_from_icor; ICOR = investment_rate / real_growth; values then compared with config/model_config.yaml A-TGT-05.
caveats: Gross ICOR ignores depreciation; net ICOR reported with PIM depreciation when capital stock is available
Sensitive to capacity utilisation, investment lags, public capex execution (Agent 03/MoF) and the relative price of capital
Remittance-financed residential construction may account for a sizeable part of GFCF with low measured output response; split residential vs non-residential if NSO asset breakdown exists

structural_change_table.question: Q3
structural_change_table.sectors: NSO industry classification (ISIC Rev.4 sections A-S as published: agriculture/forestry/fishing; mining; manufacturing; electricity/gas; water/waste; construction; wholesale/retail; transport/storage; accommodation/food; information/communication; finance/insurance; real estate; professional; administrative; public administration; education; health/social work; other services), aggregated to agriculture / industry (B-F) / services (G-S) with manufacturing and electricity shown separately.
structural_change_table.splicing: GVA shares at current prices need no splicing but show a level break at rebasing (classification and coverage changes) - report both bases in the overlap FY. Constant-price sectoral series spliced per 01A-A07 section by section; aggregates of spliced components will not equal spliced total (non-additivity) - the discrepancy is reported, not forced to zero.
structural_change_table.fy_labelling: All rows labelled by ending calendar year of Nepal FY (e.g. FY2017/18 -> '2018' only in machine fields, with 'FY2017/18' retained in display). NLFS survey periods mapped to the FY they fall in, documented per round.
method: ProductionAccounts.sector_shares() (src.economic_model.accounts) for GVA shares per FY, with production_gdp identity check (taxes less subsidies on products supplied)
Shift-share: d ln(Y/L) = sum_i [s_i,0 * d(y_i)] (within) + sum_i [y_i,0 * d s_i] (between/static reallocation) + interaction, on constant-price GVA and employment for the same FY pairs
Employment and GVA must be on the same FY and NA vintage; census usual-activity and NLFS current-activity points are not combined in one shift-share pair
known_issues: Concept break NLFS 2008 (pre-19th ICLS; own-use production work counted as employment) vs NLFS 2017/18 (19th ICLS) - large mechanical fall in agricultural employment possible; bridge using NLFS 2017/18 tabulation under both concepts if published
NLSS IV is not a labour force survey (10B)
ILO modelled sector shares are calendar-year and model-imputed between surveys - cross-check only (C-07)
